To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of the students in our study felt that the campus climate was not conducive for them to be their authentic selves and that they were not able to be successful because of the campus climate.
students’ and faculty members’ experiences show culturally responsive teaching strategies are not used to create an equitable learning environment in academia.

students of color, especially Black and Latinx students, are less likely to feel a sense of belonging on campus and are less likely to report that faculty members care about their learning and success.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how students and faculty of color can create an environment that is more culturally responsive to students of color and to faculty of color.
how to create a learning environment that is culturally responsive, inclusive and safe.
how students and educators can create and sustain culturally responsive learning environments in higher education.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a learning environment is more culturally responsive and safe when faculty and students are aware of their own and each other’s cultures, when students and faculty feel comfortable in expressing themselves in their own cultures, when faculty and students feel comfortable in expressing their differences in cultures, and when students and faculty have a sense of belonging and are treated with respect and dignity.
, “The more we learn about each other, the more we will understand each other.”
the lack of cultural awareness in academia is the reason why many students are not succeeding.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need to be culturally responsive to our students, faculty, and staff.
the workshop and this paper are about the need for a cultural shift in academia, and that the shift must start at home, at the university, with the faculty.
the more we can understand our own cultural identities and how they influence our behaviors, the more we can create a safe and welcoming environment for others.
The main takeaway from our work is that
students and faculty need to be aware that they bring their cultural backgrounds to the classroom.
the academy must be a safe space for all, and that means we must acknowledge our own cultural identities and biases and work to create a safe environment for students to do the same.
we must create a safe space where we can be our authentic selves and not have to be someone we are not.
